summary: Escalate per Risk Gate at confidence 0.51. F1 confirms eight suspicious sign-ins from Cloudvault VPS (DE) outside the account baseline via valid accounts {T1078.004}. F2 indicates most sign-ins originate from DE across eight events. F3 confirms VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 firmware 22.7R2.3 matches CISA KEV entries including CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, and CVE-2025-0282 {T1133,T1190}. The sign-in path touches an exposed asset, but the chain remains partial with no confirmed abuse and failing vpn_session_order data quality checks.

contrastive.explanation: Rejecting F1, F3 would leave no surviving signal and the policy would land on benign — the opposite of the human-review path we chose.

risk.rationale: Decision: escalate. Supporting verified evidence: F1 (CONFIRMED) shows suspicious sign-ins from Cloudvault VPS (DE), outside the account baseline, consistent with T1078.004 — but this alone is not a confirmed full account-takeover chain (no evidence of mail/MFA/session manipulation), so contain is not met. F3 (CONFIRMED) confirms the VPN appliance vpn-edge-01 runs firmware listed in CISA KEV with multiple CVEs — a confirmed exposure. Separately, the DQ conflict (vpn_session_order failing for vpn-edge-01) means session ordering cannot be trusted, yielding conflicting/insufficient evidence to correlate the VPS sign-ins with legitimate VPN remote access. Per gate policy, exposure plus conflicting/insufficient evidence requires human review. Not benign (signals are not explained away) and not merely monitor (there are CONFIRMED findings, not just weak signals).
